clue.text: Bosses' exclusion of yob that's drunk wine, wasting hours

indicators.note: the yob has swallowed the wine, so one piece goes down inside the other

parts.note: a yob is a lout, a loutish youth

indicators.note: wasting means losing something, here the abbreviation for hours is dropped

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: A boozy hooligan who has wasted his time drinking wine, with no mention of employers at all until the definition.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK loses H ('wasting hours') to give OCK, which 'that's drunk' puts inside LOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: When employers shut workers out of the workplace during a dispute, that exclusion is called a lockout.

clue.text: Grounds surrounding West Sussex market town

indicators.note: surrounding tells us the sediment word goes round the compass letter

parts.note: grounds, as in coffee grounds, are dregs or lees

explanation.surface: Reads as a description of land around a town in West Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Sussex' looks like the county name, but West only gives W: LEWES is in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, a historic market town.

clue.text: Where those drinking from tinnies gather for song?

definitions.text: Where those drinking from tinnies gather for song?

parts.words: Where those drinking from tinnies gather for song?
parts.note: a place for drinkers of tinned beer would be a '...', which split differently is an Italian word for a song

explanation.surface: Beer drinkers with cans gathering for a sing-song.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinnies are cans of beer; a zone where they gather is a CAN ZONE, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A canzone is an Italian or Provençal song or ballad, also a lyric poem form.

clue.text: Egg and something greasy served up in meat dish

parts.note: an egg is round like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: oil is a greasy substance

explanation.surface: A cook adding egg and fat to a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns OIL to LIO in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish and Portuguese stew of meat and vegetables, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Enquire: "A fee, possibly?" — you once having penned that poem

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so the old pronoun goes round the rest

parts.note: thee is an archaic form of you

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a fee is due for a poem they wrote long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ENQUIRE A FEE to FAERIEQUEEN, and 'having penned' puts that between THE and E of THEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser's long allegorical Elizabethan epic is titled The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Old publisher, strange breed never boozing

indicators.note: strange shows the letters of breed are to be made odd, rearranged

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who never drinks alcohol

explanation.surface: An eccentric publisher from a teetotal family.
explanation.definitionFit: John Debrett was an eighteenth-century London publisher, known for his guides to the peerage.

clue.text: Upsets in party — then see a mob bustle about

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: about means around and astir, telling us to shuffle these letters

explanation.surface: Trouble at a party as a crowd jostles around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A MOB BUSTLE into MBOBULATES, which follows DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: To discombobulate someone is to disconcert or confuse them, a jocular synonym of upsetting.

clue.text: Wicked stabber may land on one

definitions.text: Wicked stabber may land on one

indicators.note: wicked here means twisted or perverse, so the letters of stabber are reworked

explanation.surface: A murderous knifeman's blow landing on a victim's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' rearranges STABBER to BREASTB, then ONE is added as it stands; the whole clue also describes where the blade lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum, the flat bone at the front of the chest, is where a stab might strike.

clue.text: I shout, it is said, and watch closely

indicators.note: it is said tells us we hear the words rather than read them

parts.note: the letter I sounds like eye, and to shout is to bawl

explanation.surface: Someone yelling and keeping a sharp lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them intently, an informal verb for close scrutiny.

clue.text: One girl in exam is neater than all the rest

indicators.note: in places the numeral and the name inside the exam word

parts.note: an exam is a test
I is the Roman numeral for one
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl sitting an exam is the tidiest of the candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neatest of all is the superlative of tidy, the most orderly.

clue.text: Comes first, eats inside — problem with digestion?

indicators.note: inside says the eating word sits within the winning word

parts.note: to come first in a race is to win, so wins
to eat a meal is to dine

explanation.surface: A competitive eater who wins but then suffers indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Windiness means flatulence, an uncomfortable digestive complaint; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: In the finish this person is correct

indicators.note: In shows the pronoun placed inside the finishing word

parts.note: the finish is the end
this person, the speaker, refers to me

explanation.surface: Someone insisting that in the end they are right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' looks like an adjective, but is the verb: to emend a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing errors, a verb used of editing.

clue.text: Be disloyal to work — keep quiet at first

indicators.note: at first says the call for silence goes ahead of the work piece

parts.note: sh is the instruction to keep quiet
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Advice to a would-be traitor at work: say nothing at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police or authorities.

clue.text: Former PM's about to have drink, making a series of notes

parts.note: John Major was UK Prime Minister 1990-97, plus the possessive S
C is short for circa, Latin for about
ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A former prime minister having a pint while writing memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' sounds like written memos but means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A major scale is a sequence of eight musical notes in a set pattern of tones and semitones.

clue.text: Excursion transporting a hundred female partners to watch men? Rascals!

indicators.note: transporting means carrying, so the outing word carries the numeral within

parts.note: a sally is a trip or excursion
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of footballers, who watch their men play

explanation.surface: A coach trip carrying a hundred footballers' partners to a match, deemed rascals.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is a British tabloid acronym for wives and girlfriends of famous sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rogue, so the plural names a group of rascals.

clue.text: Old trader in posh car going to meet the Queen

indicators.note: going to meet places the royal cipher right after the car

parts.note: a Merc is short for a Mercedes, a luxury car
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A merchant arriving in a smart car for an audience with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer was historically a dealer in textiles, especially fine silks and velvets.

clue.text: Ornament — spot one to be collected

indicators.note: collected means gathered up, so the stain word gathers in the other pieces

parts.note: a blot is a spot or stain
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ornament with a mark on it, one of a set to be collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibelot is a small decorative trinket or curio, a type of ornament.

clue.text: What you do when going to a bishop for pardon

indicators.note: going to means being added to, so the solver's activity follows the first two pieces

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
what you, the solver, do with this puzzle is solve it

explanation.surface: Visiting a bishop to seek forgiveness, as in confession.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to set them free from guilt, to forgive or pardon them.

clue.text: A phoney party leader being sheepish?

parts.note: a sham is something phoney, a fake
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A fake political leader feeling embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sheepish means embarrassed by guilt, close in sense to abashed.

clue.text: Country fellow's upset about ancient city, one going under

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed fellow's goes round the rest
upset in a down entry means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: going under puts the numeral beneath the city in this down entry

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A countryman upset about a lost city sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MANS to SNAM, which goes 'about' URI.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, now Suriname, is a South American nation on the northern coast.

clue.text: Party to entertain province's exile

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the party word holds the province inside

parts.note: a bash is a party
NI stands for Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A party hosted for someone exiled from the province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exile' here is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel them from a country, to exile them.

clue.text: Bird observed on promontory

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, observed
a bill is a narrow promontory, as in Portland Bill

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spotting a bird on a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawbill is a diving duck such as the merganser, with a serrated beak.

clue.text: Report of model well above size zero brings confusion

indicators.note: report of means the model's name is heard, not seen

parts.note: Elizabeth Hurley is an English model and actress
size zero is very thin, so well above it is big and burly

explanation.surface: Tabloid news of a curvy model causing a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurly-burly is a noisy commotion, a scene of turmoil and disorder.

clue.text: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city

definitions.text: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city

parts.words: A bird such as this may be seen in Egyptian city
parts.note: putting the letter A before this water bird gives the Egyptian city on the Nile with its high dam

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's tip for a trip along the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus the bird spells ASWAN, an Egyptian city, so the bird is literally 'seen in' the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked white water bird appears in the Egyptian city's name after a single A.

clue.text: Name of political leader wanting Right to oust Left in the country

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out and replace, so one letter takes another's place

parts.note: Nigel Farage, then leader of UKIP

explanation.surface: A political leader who wants the right wing to defeat the left in his country.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage was UKIP leader; swapping L for R gives the African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African nation, named after its great river.

clue.text: Type of biscuit containers in kitchen knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: pans are cooking containers

explanation.surface: Biscuits in tins tipped over in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp brittle biscuit, so snap names that kind.

clue.text: Bright bunch of blokes with a certain sort of appeal

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A clever group of attractive men.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is a society for people with high IQs, a club of intelligent people.

clue.text: Getting bigger, no longer needs looking after

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
tending means looking after, caring for

explanation.surface: A child who is growing up and no longer needs care.
explanation.definitionFit: Extending means lengthening or enlarging, growing in size.

clue.text: Estate workers catching salmon primarily in river

indicators.note: in sets the workers and their fish within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one on the England-Wales border

indicators.note: catching means the workers enclose what they catch

parts.note: men can mean workers, as in management and men

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the fish

explanation.surface: Estate workers fishing for salmon on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord for his own use, a manor's estate.

clue.text: More flexible meal deal finally being introduced

indicators.note: introduced means put in, so the last letter goes into the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of deal

explanation.surface: A cheaper, more flexible meal offer being launched.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means bending easily, so the comparative is more pliable.
